title: Google Cogentic AI Releases 6 Math Papers in One Day
summary: Google's Cogentic multi-agent system running on Gemini 4 published six mathematical papers on November 25, including a proven factoring algorithm.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Google Research published six AI-generated math papers on November 25 from Cogentic, its multi-agent system running on Gemini 4.
- Claims include a proven subexponential factoring algorithm, improved discrete-log bounds, and breakthrough results in game theory and communication complexity.
- All papers come with promised Lean 4 formalizations for computer verification, though peer review and formal proof releases are still pending.


Google Research has officially released six mathematical research papers produced entirely by Cogentic, its multi-agent AI system for mathematical discovery. All six papers were posted to Google's public GitHub repository on November 25, 2026, marking one of the most ambitious single-day releases of AI-generated mathematical research to date. The papers span number theory, cryptography, game theory, and computational complexity, with several claiming to advance problems that have remained unsolved for decades.


## What Cogentic Is and How It Works


Cogentic is a multi-agent framework first described in a September 2026 arXiv paper by researchers from Google Research and Google DeepMind. Unlike single-model approaches that attempt to generate proofs in one pass, Cogentic divides mathematical research tasks among specialized agents. Some agents construct proofs, others act as adversarial verifiers attempting to find flaws, while additional agents handle literature review, strategic oversight, and final paper composition. The system runs on Gemini 4 as its base model, part of the Gemini 4 family that has positioned Google near the top of AI leaderboards throughout late 2026.


According to Google, each of the six papers, along with a full computer-checked version of its proof in the Lean 4 proof assistant, was entirely obtained by Cogentic with no human interaction beyond the initial prompt requesting a proof and formalization. This marks a step beyond Google DeepMind's earlier AI co-mathematician, which was designed as a human collaborator, and extends the work of AlphaProof Nexus, which solved nine open Erdős problems earlier in 2026.


## Release Date and Availability


The six papers were officially released on November 25, 2026, through Google Research's public GitHub repository. While the papers themselves are now available for review, Google has stated that the complete Lean 4 formalizations will follow in companion submissions. These machine-checkable proofs will allow the mathematical community to verify the claims computationally, a standard that has gained traction following recent AI-generated mathematical results.


## The Integer Factoring Algorithm Breakthrough


The headline paper claims a deterministic subexponential integer-factoring algorithm in the L\[1/3\] complexity class with no unproven assumptions. Integer factorization, the problem of breaking a number into its prime factors, underpins RSA encryption security. The fastest practical method, the number field sieve from around 1990, operates in the L\[1/3\] class but relies on unproven conjectures about number behavior. Previous algorithms with fully proven guarantees operated in noticeably slower complexity classes.


Cogentic's paper presents an algorithm that factors every whole number in the L\[1/3\] class with rigorous proof, verifying each prime output with a standard primality test. The constant attached to the guarantee is 105, substantially larger than the number field sieve's approximately 1.9, meaning this is a theoretical advance rather than a practical threat to current encryption. The result arrives weeks after Google DeepMind demonstrated AI-accelerated attacks on legacy RSA-1024 and after Claude assisted in factoring the 270-digit RSA-896 challenge.


## Discrete Logarithm and Game Theory Advances


A second paper addresses the discrete logarithm problem for small-characteristic finite fields, presenting a fully proven algorithm that operates slightly below the quasi-polynomial speed class. This refines the proven speed limit for a problem area already considered broken for cryptographic use, though it does not threaten encryption systems currently deployed.


In algorithmic game theory, Cogentic introduces MaximinKiteNE, an algorithm that computes approximate Nash equilibria with worst-case regret reduced from roughly one-third to one-fifth of maximum payoff. For years, efficient algorithms could not guarantee better than 0.33 regret bounds, making this reduction to 0.2 a significant advancement in a field accustomed to incremental progress. The result has practical implications for auction design, market mechanisms, and online platform optimization.


## Communication Complexity and Graph Theory Results


The fifth paper claims to break the square-root barrier for the log-rank conjecture, a central open problem in communication complexity that has stood since Shachar Lovett's 2014 bound. While the improvement in the exponent is small, five millionths, breaking a decade-long barrier is typically the hardest step in theoretical computer science, often opening the path for larger improvements.


The final paper extends a 1977 result on graph reconstruction, proving that graphs with at least 1,000 times as many connections as points can be uniquely reconstructed from the collection of all single-edge-deleted subgraphs. This advances progress on the 1964 Harary conjecture, though the full conjecture for sparser graphs remains open.


## Verification Status and Community Response


None of the six papers has undergone peer review yet. While Google states that complete Lean 4 formalizations exist for every proof, these have not been publicly released. Once available, the formalizations will enable automated verification, substantially simplifying the validation process compared to traditional hand-written proofs. The same transparency standard was adopted when a startup recently proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture with an accompanying Lean proof.


The release arrives during a remarkable period for AI mathematics. OpenAI published over 300 mathematical results from an internal model in October 2026, and this week Anthropic and OpenAI posted competing proofs of VP not equal to VNP within hours of each other. Fields Medalist Richard Borcherds recently stated that AI is now superior to him at research and teaching, while Terence Tao has cautioned that AI-produced proofs could harm the field if they arrive as opaque black boxes. Cogentic's papers, which include human-readable arguments and promised machine-checkable proofs, represent the more transparent end of this spectrum.


## What This Means


If the papers withstand scrutiny, Google will have demonstrated that multi-agent AI systems can produce significant mathematical research at scale. The November 25 release represents a qualitative shift from AI as a tool for human mathematicians to AI as an autonomous research producer. The inclusion of Lean 4 formalizations, once released, will set a verification standard that could define how AI-generated mathematical claims are evaluated. For cryptography, the factoring result confirms long-standing practitioner assumptions with rigorous proof, while for theoretical computer science, the communication complexity breakthrough opens a path others may widen. The coming months will determine whether these papers mark a turning point in mathematical research methodology.
